text: `cat /opt/scripts/tally-processed.sh` -- there's no bug in the arithmetic itself. Try running it several times back-to-back by hand: it behaves fine. The problem only shows up when more than one copy is running *at the same time*.

Look at the timing: the script sleeps for half a second between reading the counter and writing it back, and cron fires it every minute regardless of whether the previous run finished. If a run ever takes long enough to still be alive when the next one starts, both copies read the same starting value before either has written anything back.

That's a classic read-modify-write race: two overlapping runs both read `count=N`, both compute `N+1`, and whichever writes last wins -- the other run's increment is silently lost. Nothing errors, the file is never corrupted syntactically, it's just numerically wrong.

Fix it by serializing access with a real lock, not just moving the sleep around -- a timing tweak only narrows the window, it doesn't close it. Use `flock` around the read-modify-write in `/opt/scripts/tally-processed.sh` itself, e.g. `exec 9>/tmp/tally-processed.lock` followed by `flock -x 9` near the top of the script, before the counter is ever read. `flock -x` blocks until it gets the lock, so a second invocation simply waits its turn instead of racing.
